assumptions.description: US NHANES, Finnish Health2011 and Iranian Kerman components are transported into the Mexico equal-cell analytical design; country, ethnicity, calendar and survey-design differences remain unresolved.

Source prior-diagnosis, medication, HbA1c selection and fasting-duration restrictions may differ from the task. Finnish HbA1c>=6.5/medication exclusions and Kerman known-diabetes inclusion are not imposed on generated rows. No target anemia/medication exclusion is invented.

HbA1c assay percentages and plasma/serum glucose components are treated as sufficiently commensurable for this working law. Compartment/assay equivalence is unverified; reported source contexts remain intact.
Exactly375 rows per sex-age cell; integer ages uniform within25-39,40-54,55-69,70-79. Fixed equal-cell design is not a national survey or source-population replay.
Combine NHANES BMI mean28.01 with Kerman marginal SD3.8; scaled-beta support10-65 kg/m^2 and independence from age/sex are assumptions, not target eligibility or measured null relationships.
Finnish binary-age-adjusted slopes transfer to continuous-age adjustment; common main effects extend25-79 without interactions despite contextual heterogeneity.
Approximately8mg/dL source age contrast divided by an assumed40-year span yields the working0.20mg/dL/year glucose-age slope. The source did not report that per-year coefficient.

S1 displayed block lists age+sex+BMI, whereas article Methods says glucose analyses also adjust fasting duration. The coefficient is used despite this unresolved adjustment difference; no fasting covariate or matching operator is invented.
Transfer Kerman marginal Pearson r0.23 to the full equal-cell distribution. It is never relabelled partial correlation; its change under altered covariates/selection is unmeasured.

NHANES50-54 mean5.40 and97.5th percentile6.0 define approximate marginal SD(6-5.4)/1.959963984540054 by a normal-shape assumption. This is not SE-to-SD conversion. Subtract model explained variation for constant conditional H variance.
Reference ages50-54 uniform and sex balanced with proposed BMI/glucose law approximate unreported source joint covariates; no simulated source table or valid source replay is claimed.

Heterogeneous source components are assumed jointly compatible in one linear-conditional-mean law. Scalar algebra checks mathematical compatibility only; decomposition is statistical, not causal mediation.

Finnish S1/S2 outcomes are inferred as mmol/L and HbA1c percent from article context; raw supplement coefficients retain unit not_reported. Rounded18.0 converts mmol/L to mg/dL and sex contrasts reverse male-minus-female to female. Source per-year/per-BMI coefficients rescale by10/5 for requested terms. These are declared derivations, not source labels.

Scaled-beta BMI, conditional beta glucose on(0,126), and conditional beta HbA1c on(0,100) are working laws. All moments finite; no HbA1c6.5 exclusion. Independent draws conditional on covariates except fixed stratum quotas. Floating-point endpoint guards are numerical only.

Parameters are fixed conditional on source transports. Individual residual variation and Monte Carlo seeds do not represent calibrated source/model/transport uncertainty. No confidence score or p-value weight is used.

design.derivation: Task-mandated equal sex-age quotas; uniform within-band age assumed. Population age moments calculated from inclusive integer bands, never from a realized draw.

bmi.derivation: Mean28.01 from NHANES; individual marginal SD3.8 from Kerman. Bounds10/65 assumed. Beta mean fraction p=(28.01-10)/55; concentration(28.01-10)*(65-28.01)/3.8^2-1. No SE substitution.

glucose.derivation: Mean91.2 and marginal SD12.4 transferred from Kerman. Raw Finnish0.0240 and0.2472 have absent units; infer mmol/L under A_units, multiply18.0, reverse male contrast =>0.432 and-4.4496. Age0.20=approximately8/assumed40. Upper126 from task. Concentration partitions marginal variance into covariate mean variance and beta residual variance, using reviewed algebra.

hba1c.derivation: Reference age50-54 mean5.40 and upperquantile6.0; normal z(.975) supplies approximate within-band marginal SD, not SE. Raw Finnish BMI0.0125 and male-0.0230 outcome units inferred as percent; reverse sex to+0.0230 total female slope. Age0.010 from NHANES adjusted coefficient. Marginal r0.23 from Kerman stays marginal. Solve signed moment equation with proposed G/B/age moments and reference H variance for conditional glucose coefficient c and residual variance. Reviewed c=0.0028039450477448575, residual variance0.09002838407739247; conditional BMI=.0125-c*.432; female=.023-c*(-4.4496). Physical percentage upper100 is assumed support. Generator derives these from specification, not realized rows.
